title: Artificial Intelligence Based Home OCT Management of Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Faricimab Treated Eyes
content:
Background and Objectives: Individual variability in neovascular Age-related Macular degeneration (nAMD) activity makes it difficult to optimize injection timing, often leading to either under or over treatment. The objective was to report the first cohort of previously-treated patients who were switched to faricimab and managed exclusively by Home OCT (HOCT)-guided office visits for 12 months enabling highly personalized injection intervals. 
Materials and Methods: Prospective interventional cohort study. Treatment decisions were based on HOCT alerts and in-office examinations. Main Outcome Measures: HOCT adherence, injections intervals; change in VA; comparison to preceding period and standard-of-care simulated intervals; predictability of intervals; spatial location of reactivations; fluid accumulation rates.
Results: Twelve participants with at least one eye undergoing anti-VEGF treatment enrolled. Mean age 75.0 years; 58% male. 6,057 scans performed, (mean of 252.4 ± 110.2 scans/eye; 5.51 ± 1.48 scans/week). Among 9 faricimab-treated eyes, 48 injections were administered. Mean inter-injection interval increased from 6.0±1.7 weeks pre-study to 10.8±3.0 weeks during study (p=0.008). Compared to 85 injections projected under the HMO specific T&E schedule, HOCT guidance had potential to reduce injection burden by 44% (p=0.004). Mean VA change was -0.00 ± 0.15 LogMAR. Correlation between consecutive intervals was 0.18, p=0.289. Median similarity of relative fluid distribution was 0.95. Mean and median total-fluid accumulation rate were 3.4 ± 3.2 nL/day and 2.6 nL/day (IQR 1.1–3.9 nL/day) respectively. SRF accumulation rate was 2.9 nL/day higher than IRF rate (p=0.001). For every additional 1 nL of total fluid volume, daily total-fluid accumulation rate increased by 0.06 nL/day (95% CI 0.04–0.08, p=4.64×10⁻⁹) thus, larger total-fluid burdens were associated with faster fluid accumulation.
Conclusions: HOCT-guided personalized management of nAMD eyes with faricimab is feasible and achieved significant reduction in injection burden with larger individualized intervals compared to T&E treatment. HOCT monitoring reveals new insights, supporting personalized management.
